turns.t: Morning, doctor. I'm Bridie, Callum's foster carer. He needs this medical form completed for the apprenticeship, and he's a bit nervous.
I'm not nervous. I just don't like doctors. ~
Fair enough, Callum, I'll make it as painless as I can. It's a standard form, so I need to ask about your health. How are you generally? ~
Fine. ~
He gets headaches, doctor. He doesn't tell people.
Callum, do you get headaches?
Sometimes. Not a big deal.
How long have you had them?
Dunno. A while.
I'm not sure either, I've only had him two years, and he had them when he came to me. I can't say when they began.
That's fine, I'll write that the start isn't known. Do you get anything with them, sickness, flashing lights?
No. Just a headache.
And do your knees or joints hurt, when you run or do sport?
My left knee. When I play football. It clicks.
Any chest pain or fainting, ever?
No. Never.
Good. For the form, I'll fill in the rest from your school health records. Is that all right? ~
Okay. ~
Your hearing and eye checks at school were fine, I see. ~
He's had his jabs, they're all up to date. I've got the red book. ~
Thank you, Bridie. Callum, what's the apprenticeship in? ~
Joinery. ~
That's a good trade. You'll need to wear ear protection, and goggles, and not lift anything too heavy until you've been trained.
I know. ~
Your knee clicking, any pain on stairs, or does it give way? ~
No. It just clicks. ~
That's common, and not usually a problem. If it starts to swell, lock, or give way, come and see me.
Okay. ~
On the headaches, keep a note of when they happen and what you were doing, in case it's tiredness or screens.
I'll help him with that. ~
I'll complete the form for you now, and it'll be ready at the front desk tomorrow. ~
Thank you, doctor. ~
Can I go now? ~
You can, Callum. Good luck with the apprenticeship. ~
